draft.emotion: frustrated and blank, searching the mind for a missing thought
notes: Use 'olvidar' when you simply forget something, but use 'olvidarse de' when you fail to remember or leave something behind on purpose or by mistake.
When something escapes your memory entirely, it is very common to use the reflexive form 'olvidarse': 'Se me olvidó las llaves' (I forgot my keys).

senses.definition: Not to remember something or to let it slip from your mind.

examples.text: Siempre suelo olvidar las fechas de los cumpleaños.
examples.translation: I always tend to forget birthday dates.
examples.emotion: apologetic and sheepish, admitting a common absent-minded mistake

senses.definition: Leave something behind somewhere by mistake.

examples.text: Voy a volver al restaurante porque creo que olvidé mi paraguas.
examples.translation: I am going to go back to the restaurant because I think I left my umbrella behind.
examples.emotion: annoyed and rushing back to retrace steps
